title.value: Learning adversarially robust kernel ensembles with kernel average pooling
title.justification: The paper focuses on introducing Kernel Average Pooling (KAP) as a method to improve adversarial robustness in neural networks by learning kernel ensembles.
title.quote: We introduce Kernel Average Pooling (KAP), a neural network building block that applies the mean filter along the kernel dimension of the layer activation tensor.

analysis.description: This paper introduces Kernel Average Pooling (KAP) as a novel method to enhance adversarial robustness in convolutional neural networks. KAP operates by averaging the activation kernels within each layer, forming kernel ensembles that improve robustness against input perturbations and adversarial attacks. The research empirically demonstrates substantial robustness improvements without adversarial training, evaluated on datasets like CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Imagenet. The results suggest that KAP acts as a computationally efficient alternative to traditional adversarial training techniques.

type.justification: The paper conducts empirical evaluations to demonstrate the effectiveness of Kernel Average Pooling in improving adversarial robustness across various benchmarks.
type.quote: Empirical evaluations on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImagenet, and Imagenet datasets show substantial improvements in robustness against strong adversarial attacks.
